sections_inspected: Religious and Secular Critique of Money
The Unbounding of Markets as the Basis of Modern Capitalism
The Intransparency of World Society to Itself: Luhmann and Hayek
The Religious Worldview and the Consequences of Its Dethronement
Universalism and the Contingency of the World: A Comparative Perspective on Capitalism and Religion
scope_outcomes.criterion: An eligible finding identifies an expressly announced or stated change in a concept’s use, including adaptation, narrowing, or application to a new purpose.
scope_outcomes.basis: The inspected text explicitly redirects theological money critique into sociology, applies Luhmann’s self-description to market ideology, extends Weber’s Protestant-ethic finding to non-Christian religions, and reworks religious Kingdom-of-God imagery to characterize capitalist growth.
limitations: Some transfers are presented through cited scholarship or analogy, so the text alone cannot establish all intermediary transmission paths.

evidence_state.coverage_basis: reader/reviewer report; source bytes do not establish inspection or completeness
